tasks.title: Decide the fate of resolveAnthropicApiKeyChain — no production callers remain
tasks.description: Task #51 deleted warnIfLegacyApiKey and its two call sites (src/commands/narrate.ts, src/commands/run.ts), which were the only consumers of resolveAnthropicApiKeyChain(). The function is still exported from src/config.ts and covered by test/config.test.ts, but nothing in src/ calls it — the resolution is now purely documentary, mirroring the same chain in lib/cairn_narrate_server.py (see task #59). Either (a) delete the helper, its AnthropicApiKeyResolution type, and its tests, leaving the Python server as the single implementation, or (b) keep it and give it a real caller — e.g. have runNarrate/runRun pass the resolved key into the narration server env instead of relying on the child process re-reading the environment. Do NOT normalize onto plain ANTHROPIC_API_KEY under either option: the loop deliberately blanks that name to force Max-plan usage. Sequence this after #59 so both sides of the mirror are decided together.
tasks.notes:
# Task #66 — Fate of `resolveAnthropicApiKeyChain`

## Status: code work is DONE and was already committed (706e1a3, iteration 16)

Iteration 17 found nothing left to implement. This iteration re-verified the prior
iteration's work from scratch rather than trusting its notes, and diagnosed why the
task kept bouncing back to in-progress. **The bounce is a cairn bug, not a code
problem** — see the last section.

## Decision: option (a) — deleted the helper

Reasoning, so nobody re-litigates it:

1. **Option (b) would have had no behavioral effect.** Its premise was "pass the
   resolved key into the narration server env instead of relying on the child
   re-reading the environment." But `startNarrationServer()` (`src/narration.ts`)
   spawns the Python server with `{ detached: true, stdio: 'ignore' }` and **no `env`
   option**, so the child inherits the parent's `process.env` verbatim. The
   `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` blanking is *per-spawn and non-mutating* — every site builds a
   fresh object (`{ ...process.env, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: '' }` in `run.ts`, `plan.ts`,
   `summarize.ts`, `post-task-reviewer.ts`); the parent's own `process.env` is never
   touched. The narration server already sees the real key under whichever name the
   user exported.
2. **Option (b) could not have collapsed the mirror either.** `lib/cairn_narrate_server.py`
   is a standalone `argparse` script that can be launched directly, so it must keep its
   own resolution chain regardless. (b) would have left two implementations *plus* new
   env plumbing; (a) leaves exactly one, sited where the key is actually consumed.

## Changes (all in commit 706e1a3)

- **`src/config.ts`** — deleted the `AnthropicApiKeyResolution` interface,
  `resolveAnthropicApiKeyChain()`, and its doc comment. `setConfigEnvVars()` is now the
  last export in the file.
- **`test/config.test.ts`** — deleted the 6-test `describe('resolveAnthropicApiKeyChain')`
  block and dropped the symbol from the top-level import.
- **`lib/cairn_narrate_server.py`** (~line 224) — the comment above the key resolution
  said "Mirrors `resolveAnthropicApiKeyChain()` in `src/config.ts`", which this task
  turned into a dangling reference. Rewritten to state that this is now the *only*
  implementation and that the TypeScript side deliberately has none, and to absorb the
  "never normalize the resolved value back onto plain `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`" invariant
  that previously lived only in the deleted TS docstring. That invariant is load-bearing
  (it is what preserves Max-plan forcing), so it needed a new home rather than being
  deleted with its old one.
- **`src/commands/narrate.ts`, `src/commands/run.ts`** — listed in the task's `files`
  but needed **no change**. Task #51 had already removed `warnIfLegacyApiKey` and both
  call sites; neither file imports from `../config` today. Verified, not assumed.

## Verification (re-run fresh in iteration 17)

- `grep -rn "resolveAnthropicApiKeyChain\|AnthropicApiKeyResolution" .` across the whole
  repo (excluding `.git`, `node_modules`, `.cairn`) → **zero hits, exit 1**. No dangling
  references in code, tests, or prose.
- `bun build --target=bun src/index.ts --outfile /tmp/cairn-healthcheck` from the
  **project root** → clean, 0.43 MB entry point.
- `bun test` from the **project root** → **799 pass, 0 fail, 29 files**. Task #65's
  baseline was 805; exactly 6 tests were removed, 805 − 6 = 799. No collateral breakage.
- Did **not** modify `cairn.json`'s `healthCheck` and did **not** run `./install.sh`,
  per the pin/unpin procedure in CLAUDE.md.

## Why this task kept reverting — read this before re-doing any work

Both the "BUILD HEALTH CHECK FAILED: FileNotFound opening root directory `src`" banner
and the "Post-iteration test validation failed" revert are the same cairn bug, and both
are **false**. Task #66's `directory` is `src`, and:

- `src/health-check.ts:55` — `cwd = taskDir ? join(projectRoot, taskDir) : projectRoot`,
  then runs the project-wide `healthCheck` there. From `<root>/src`, the root-relative
  `src/index.ts` does not exist. Cosmetic: it only prints a scary banner.
- `src/test-validator.ts:94` — `const cwd = path.resolve(projectRoot, taskDir)`, then
  runs each entry of the task's `tests` array there. From `<root>/src`,
  `bun test test/config.test.ts` matches nothing. Bun's stderr ("29 files were searched"
  / "note: Tests need \".test\"...") matches none of `CANT_RUN_PATTERNS`, so
  `isCantRunError()` returns false and the failure is classified as a **real** test
  failure → `fileTask.status = 'in-progress'`. **This is what reverted #66 twice.**

Filed as task **#68** (originally health-check only). Iteration 17 appended a note
extending #68's scope to `src/test-validator.ts` with the full diagnosis.

**Livelock warning for the loop:** #66 is priority 16 and #68 is priority 20, so #66
outranks #68 and will be re-selected and re-reverted indefinitely until #68 lands. If
you are an agent handed #66 again: nothing is wrong with the code — go fix #68
(`src/health-check.ts` + `src/test-validator.ts`, both cwd → `projectRoot`), then #66
will stick.

## Remaining work

Task **#68** is still pending, so `.cairn_complete` was **not** created.

tasks.title: Health check runs from the task directory, so root-relative healthCheck commands fail spuriously
tasks.description: src/health-check.ts:55 computes `cwd = taskDir ? join(projectRoot, taskDir) : projectRoot` and runs the project-level `healthCheck` command there. But `healthCheck` is a single project-wide string in cairn.json, written relative to the project root — cairn's own is `bun build --compile src/index.ts --outfile /tmp/cairn-healthcheck`. For any task whose `directory` field is not the project root, that command is executed from `<root>/<directory>` and fails on paths that resolve fine from the root. Observed live in iteration 16: task #66 has `directory: "src"`, so the pre-iteration health check ran from `<root>/src`, where `src/index.ts` does not exist, and the agent was handed a `BUILD HEALTH CHECK FAILED: FileNotFound opening root directory "src"` banner describing a build that is actually green (verified: the same command from the project root succeeds). This is a false failure signal on every non-root task and wastes agent attention chasing a nonexistent break. Decide and implement one of: (a) always run `healthCheck` from `projectRoot` and drop the `taskDir` join — simplest, matches the fact that the command is project-wide; (b) keep the per-directory cwd but make it opt-in via a per-directory health check config. Prefer (a) unless there is a known consumer relying on per-directory cwd. Note that `shouldRunHealthCheck()` also probes `join(cwd, 'package.json')` for the `npm run type-check` special case and has the same cwd assumption — fix both together. Update test/health-check.test.ts to cover a non-root taskDir with a root-relative command.
tasks.notes: SCOPE EXTENSION (found in iteration 17): src/test-validator.ts:94 has the IDENTICAL cwd bug and is strictly more damaging than the health-check one. It computes `const cwd = path.resolve(projectRoot, taskDir)` and runs each entry of the task's `tests` array there. Task test commands are written root-relative (task #66's are `bun test test/config.test.ts` and `bun test`), so for any task whose `directory` is not the project root they run from <root>/<directory> and fail. Unlike the health-check case this does not merely print a scary banner — the failure falls through isCantRunError() (bun's stderr for a non-matching filter reads '29 files were searched' + 'note: Tests need ".test"...', which matches none of CANT_RUN_PATTERNS) and is classified as a REAL test failure, so validateTaskTests() reverts the task to in-progress. This reverted task #66 in iterations 16 and 17 even though `bun test` is 799 pass / 0 fail from the project root. Because #66 (priority 16) outranks #68 (priority 20), the loop will keep re-selecting #66 and reverting it — a livelock that #68 is the only fix for. Fix both files in the same pass: run project-level healthCheck and task `tests` from projectRoot, and cover a non-root taskDir with a root-relative command in test/test-validator.test.ts as well as test/health-check.test.ts.
